subject: health
essentialQuestion: Why is health so unevenly distributed across places that are only a few miles apart?

prompts.prompt: Explain air, water, housing, and neighborhood conditions as health inputs in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of food access, transportation, and distance to care.
Apply environmental hazards and how communities learn about them in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving public health functions and how a community responds to an outbreak; correct it and explain why.
Connect reading community-level health data honestly with who has standing to change a community health condition. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Analyze a fictional community health dataset, identify the two conditions with the largest effect, and write a short brief proposing one realistic intervention with its likely limits.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: Analysis may be written, charted, spoken, or completed on a supplied guided-analysis frame with the dataset pre-summarized.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
